entry.title: This site is agent-readable by default
entry.content:
This is the first note on the site, and it's also the documentation for how the site is put together. Two goals, in priority order:
1. Be trivially readable by agents. 2. Be tolerable to look at for a human who happens to visit.
Everything else follows from those.
## What "agent-readable" means here
- Every note is written in Markdown and published as Markdown at a stable URL: `/notes/<id>.md`. That file is the canonical artifact. The `.html` version is a thin render for browsers; agents should fetch the `.md`. - `/llms.txt` is an index following the [llmstxt.org](https://llmstxt.org) v2 convention: a short summary plus a list of links to the Markdown versions of every note. - `/llms-full.txt` is every note concatenated into one grep-able file. If you have no fancier tool, fetch that and grep it. - `/notes/index.json` is a machine-readable manifest with id, title, date, tags, and both URL forms for each note. - `/.well-known/agent.json` points at all of the above and declares the preferred format. - `/feed.xml` is an Atom feed whose entries carry the Markdown body in `<content type="text/markdown">`.
## What it does not do
There is no JavaScript, no tracking, no analytics, no comments, no newsletter signup, no social embeds, no cookie banner. There is no "About" page with a headshot and a career timeline. The index page is a flat list of notes with dates. That's the whole site.
## How it's built
A single Python script (`build.py`, stdlib only) reads `notes/*.md`, parses a small frontmatter block, and writes the static site into `docs/`. No framework, no dependencies, no build pipeline beyond `python3 build.py`. The source notes are the thing; everything in `docs/` is derived.
The frontmatter is intentionally simple:
``` --- title: Note Title date: 2026-11-23 tags: [ml, scaling] status: public --- ```
`status: public` is required for a note to appear in the output. Anything else (draft, private, etc.) is skipped — so drafts can live in the same `notes/` directory without being published.

entry.content:
This is a placeholder note so the site has more than one entry while you decide what to actually write about. Delete it (or set `status: draft`) once you have real content.
The convention: create a new file in `notes/`, give it a leading numeric prefix for sort order if you care, fill in the frontmatter, write Markdown below the second `---`, and run `python3 build.py`.
Slug = filename without `.md`. So `notes/0002-placeholder.md` becomes `/notes/0002-placeholder.md` and `/notes/0002-placeholder.html`.
